analysis:
The only change is in scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py, line 141 on base and lines 141-142 on head. It adds "model-requant-upload.yml" to the UNROUTED tuple. This is a test-only CI guard script with no runtime provider, coordinator, cache or attestation code.

Effect: test_every_workflow_is_classified requires every workflow file in .github/workflows to be classified, so the new workflow file must be listed or the test fails. Listing it in UNROUTED also subjects it to test_release_and_credentialed_workflows_keep_literal_runners and test_watchdog_rescues_only_this_repositorys_routed_runs. Those tests enforce:
- no reference to darkbloom-route.yml or needs.route;
- every runs-on matches ^blacksmith-[a-z0-9-]+$;
- no self-hosted or darkbloom-* labels.

This tightens the guard: a credentialed or publication workflow cannot run on routed or self-hosted Darkbloom runners. No weakening is visible, and no threat-model asset, trust boundary or mitigation in the retained definitions (T-041 is the only one supplied) is affected.

Remaining unverified: the new .github/workflows/model-requant-upload.yml is not in the supplied evidence. Whether its runs-on labels actually satisfy the literal-runner regex, and whether its credentials or secrets are handled safely, belong to a review of that workflow file. If that file is absent or non-conforming, this test would fail in CI. That is a CI failure, not a security regression.
